newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - softer tone, reassessing Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - softer tone, reassessing Fed.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were pegged flat to off one-eighth early Friday as traders fretted that remarks by Fed chief earlier this week were harsher than first thought.

"They're not quite so sure," a trader said, explaining that the market now was questioning whether it had been too quick to discount a speech by Fed chairman Greenspan on Wednesday, in which he warned of the risks of wage-driven inflation.

While the market was not looking for the central banks to tighten interest rates until evidence of inflation emerges, they said they were more pesimistic that it might need to do so over the long-term.
"If it will be in February, March, June or July, I don't know," another trader said, explaining that the market sentiment had turned bearish for the moment.

Further, traders said that expectations that the benchmark, 30-year Treasury bonds will continue to soften has discourged municipal bond issuers from tapping credit markets, and also dampened activity in the secondary market.

"No one wants to buy anything because everybody seems to think that the bond is on a path down, and it doesn't want to get it all done in one day," a trader said, explaining that yields were expected to gradually rise.

While this week has seen a sizable number of bid wanted lists being circulated, with municipal bond players focused on shortening duration by selling 30-year discount bonds, traders said that Friday was likely to see only limited selling interest as the market winds down ahead of the weekend.
Bonds that have been in demand this week in the secondary market mainly are intermediate, noncallable issues, a trader added.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, NET, and were bid at 5.85 percent, up two basis points.
And New York City Refunding of August 2025, which have a 6-1/8 percent coupon, were bid at 6.34 percent NET, up two basis points.

The March U.S. Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade fell eight ticks to 110-19/32, while the March municipal bond futures eased six ticks to 114-10/32. As a result, the MOB spread was calculated at plus 119 ticks.
